Pan-Arctic Permafrost · Crowdsourced Validation

Check Active RTS Expansion

A guide to the RTS Annotation Tool. You review the automated mapping of retrogressive thaw slumps (RTS) grid cell by grid cell — confirm whether each grid cell contains a real slump, correct the polygons where needed, and track how each slump's boundary expands across six years of Sentinel-2 imagery. Every confirmation, edit, and addition you make becomes ground reference for future mapping and model calibration.

00

Main Page

The screen has three working areas. Get oriented with these before you start.

Top bar

Global view toggles (Opacity, Show outlines, Fill, NIR, Hover preview), Reload, Undo / Redo, the grid-cell counter #/total, and Jump-to-grid-cell.

Left canvas

The year thumbnails, the large image with pre-drawn polygons, and zoom controls with a zoom lock.

Right panel

Progress and Yes / No / Unknown counts, the per-year RTS list, the drawing Tool block (with ⇄ Auto-merge), the grid-cell Note, and the Validate-Result buttons plus Save / Skip / Prev / Next.

01

Validation workflow

  1. Open a grid cell. Use the year strip (or press 1–6) to step through the same area across years and watch how the slump changes.

  2. If the grid cell already has pre-drawn polygons (unconfirmed), check each one and act on it:

    • Drawn correctly→ select the RTS and press Enter to confirm (or click its ✓ button).
    • Real RTS, but the position or shape is wrong→ adjust the boundary in Manual or Mouse mode.
    • Not a real RTS (false positive)→ delete the RTS.
    • A real RTS the model missed (false negative)→ add one using the Drawing tools.

  3. Once every year and every RTS in the grid cell is handled, click the grid-cell-level result button, then Save.

  4. Optional — if a grid cell's detections are scattered across years or fragments, run ⇄ Auto-merge to line them up in one click. See the Auto-merge section for what it does.

02

Grid cell result & navigation

Confirmed Correct RTS

The grid cell contains a real RTS and the polygons are accurate. Confirms and saves the polygons for all years.

No RTS

The grid cell contains no real RTS. Clears the polygons in every year.

Unsure

Image quality is poor or the case is ambiguous. Leaves it flagged for later review.

Save / Skip / move on. Save (S) writes your decision; Skip (Space) passes the grid cell without a verdict; ← Prev / Next → (← / →) move between grid cells. Use Jump to # in the top bar to go straight to a grid-cell number.
03

Drawing tools

SAM

Place Include (F) points inside the slump and Exclude (B) points outside it; the SAM model segments the boundary from those prompts. A few well-placed points usually beat many. Clear points drops the current prompts; Clear removes polygons.

All Years — points added on any year sync to the others and segment all six boundaries at once; This Year — segments only the current year. Matching this: Clear under All Years removes every year's polygon, under This Year only the current one.
Manual

Click to add a vertex, double-click to close the polygon, Esc to cancel. Best when the model isn't helping and you want to trace the outline by hand.

Mouse

Edit an existing polygon: left-click adds a vertex, right-click deletes the hovered vertex, and drag moves one. Delete removes the hovered vertex, or the whole RTS if you're not over a vertex.

Remember

Finish one RTS before starting the next. After you draw or segment an RTS, mark it complete by clicking its ✓ in the left RTS panel (or pressing Enter). Only then begin drawing the next one — otherwise new points keep editing the current RTS.

Same rts_id

The same rts_id must refer to the same slump in every year, so its yearly polygons trace one slump changing over time — not different features. If the automatic rts_id is wrong, edit the rts_id field in the RTS panel by hand to keep it consistent across all years.

04

Auto-merge

The ⇄ Auto-merge button consolidates each RTS's boundary as it expands across the years, in one click. Because an active retrogressive thaw slump only grows over time, the operation is strictly additive and gap-free — a later year's boundary always contains the earlier ones, no detection is dropped, and no year is left empty. It also merges scattered fragments of the same RTS within a year. Run it after you've drawn the slumps, to line up each RTS's expansion consistently through time.

Tip

Delete any RTS you don't need before running Auto-merge. Otherwise a false positive gets accumulated and force-filled into every year too, and you'll have to clean it out of all of them afterwards.

  1. Accumulate across years. From the earliest year to the latest, each rts_id (e.g. rts01) accumulates the union of its shape from all earlier years. If a year is missing that rts_id, it is force-filled with the last known shape — so no year is left blank.

  2. Merge overlaps. After accumulation, within a single year any RTSs that now touch (pixel overlap) are merged into one.

Heads up

Auto-merge affects only the current grid cell and only ever adds to later years — earlier years are never altered or shrunk. Any RTS it touches is un-confirmed and must be re-confirmed by hand. The whole action is undoable with Ctrl+Z.

05

View & RTS controls

Top-bar toggles change how the imagery and polygons are drawn — they never change your data.

OpacityBlends the imagery under the polygons so you can see the ground beneath an outline.
Show outlinesToggles the polygon outlines on or off.
FillFills each polygon with a translucent tint instead of showing only its outline.
NIRSwitches to the near-infrared composite, where fresh disturbance often stands out more clearly.
Hover previewPreviews an RTS when you hover over it in the list.
Zoom · lock− / + / RESET control zoom; the lock (🔒) keeps the same zoom and pan when you switch years so frames stay aligned.
ReloadReloads the current grid cell from the server, discarding unsaved local edits.
ThumbnailsA green border means that year already has a segmentation; the small badge is its RTS count. The last thumbnail is an animated GIF of all years.
RTS panelEach RTS shows its Area (ha / m²), a per-RTS Note, and Delete / confirm (✓) buttons. The right panel also tracks overall Progress and Yes / No / Unknown counts.
06

Keyboard shortcuts

You can validate almost entirely from the keyboard — worth learning, since a run is thousands of grid cells.

FSAM Include point
BSAM Exclude point
NNew RTS
EToggle edit mode
EnterConfirm the active RTS
DeleteDelete hovered vertex / RTS
EscCancel current drawing
1–6Switch to year 1–6
SSave the grid cell
SpaceSkip the grid cell
← →Previous / next grid cell
Ctrl+ZUndo
Ctrl+YRedo
